intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that osteogenesis imperfecta type X (OI10) is caused by homozygous mutation in the SERPINH1 gene (600943) on chromosome 11q13.5.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type X (OI10) is caused by homozygous mutation in the SERPINH1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity for a missense mutation in SERPINH1, which encodes the collagen chaperone protein HSP47, results in severe recessive osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.explanation: The paper describes homozygous SERPINH1 mutation causing recessive OI. The label 'type X/OI10' is OMIM nomenclature.

The patient was homozygous for a missense mutation in SERPINH1. Duran et al. (2015) also described OI caused by HSP47 deficiency as recessive.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with severe autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta, Christiansen et al. (2010) identified a homozygous missense mutation (c.233T-C; L78P) in the SERPINH1 gene, which encodes the collagen chaperone-like protein HSP47. The mutation caused the endoplasmic reticulum-resident HSP47 to be degraded through the proteasome. In fibroblasts from the patient, type I procollagen accumulated in the Golgi, and part of the secreted type I procollagen was protease sensitive.

paragraphs.text: Christiansen et al. (2010) found that the L78P mutation in HSP47 led to proteasomal degradation of the protein. In the patient's fibroblasts, type I procollagen accumulated in the Golgi, and part of the secreted type I procollagen was protease sensitive. The authors suggested that HSP47 monitors the integrity of the type I procollagen triple helix at the boundary between the endoplasmic reticulum and the cis-Golgi. Without HSP47, procollagen would move from the ER to the Golgi faster and its helical structure would be compromised.

paragraphs.text: Duran et al. (2015) found evidence that HSP47 and FKBP65 act cooperatively during the posttranslational maturation of type I procollagen. In cells with mutant HSP47, the two proteins did not interact properly. The authors concluded that OI caused by HSP47 deficiency and OI caused by FKBP65 deficiency share a common cellular pathway.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with severe autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta (OI10), Christiansen et al. (2010) identified a homozygous c.233T-C transition in the SERPINH1 gene, resulting in a leu78-to-pro (L78P) substitution in HSP47. The mutation caused the endoplasmic reticulum-resident HSP47 to be degraded through the proteasome. In the patient's fibroblasts, type I procollagen accumulated in the Golgi and part of the secreted type I procollagen was protease sensitive. 3-Hydroxylation of proalpha1(I) prolyl residue 986 was normal.
